fragmentPrivacy: Fragment links put the secret after # for the browser to read and calculate locally. It is not sent with the page request. The full link still contains the secret; do not share it publicly.
pathWarningRequest: The secret is in the URL path. Opening this link sends that path to the hosting service before the page can show a warning. This notice cannot block or undo that request.
pathWarningRotate: The secret may remain in hosting or proxy access logs; this does not mean someone has obtained it. We recommend generating a replacement secret in the original website or app’s two-factor settings and confirming the previous secret is invalid. Do not simply edit its characters here.
pathWarningFragment: Use a # link instead: the secret after # is not sent with the page request. The complete link may still remain in browser history; do not share it publicly.
pathWarningLimit: Switching to a # link only reduces exposure in future requests. It cannot undo previous requests or replace the secret at the original service.
linkPrivacyMechanism: The browser sends only the address before # to the server. In /2fa/SECRET, the secret is part of the request path. In /2fa#SECRET, it is a fragment read locally by the page, not included in the page request. HTTPS encrypts transport, but does not hide the path from the hosting service receiving the request.
